title: Layer-2 composed bound, base case
statement:
Let $g_1,\dots,g_m$ be DNF formulas on $n$ Boolean variables, and let $w$ be a positive integer such that every $g_i$ has width at most $w$; assume $n \ge 1$, and that in each term the literals occupy distinct positions and any two literals sharing a variable are equal (so each variable is queried at most once per term). Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on the $m$ gate-inputs whose depth is $0$ (hence a single literal), and let $F$ be the composed Boolean function on $n$ variables given by $F(x) = c\bigl(g_1(x),\dots,g_m(x)\bigr)$. Fix natural numbers $s$, $l$, $t$ with $l \ge 1$, $s \ge 1$, $w \le l$, and $\mathrm{size}(c) \le s$. Then, for a Bernoulli random restriction $\rho$ with parameter $\tfrac{1}{40l}$, the probability that the restriction of $F$ along $\rho$ — the function sending $x$ to $F$ evaluated with the coordinates fixed by $\rho$ and the free coordinates read from $x$ — has decision-tree depth exceeding $t$ is at most
\[
s\left(\tfrac12\right)^{l} + \left(\tfrac12\right)^{t} + s\,e^{-n/(120 l)} + e^{-n/(120 l)}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: family of m DNF gates g_1,...,g_m on n variables
each gate has width at most w (widthBound)
the width bound w is positive (widthPos)
in each term, literals sharing a variable are equal (varInj)
each term has no repeated literal (nodup)
depth(c) + 2 <= 2, i.e. c has depth 0, a single literal (hd_depth)
replaced:
Base case ($d_{\mathrm{inner}} = 2$) of the composed layer-2 bound. Here the top circuit
$c_{\mathrm{top}}$ has depth $0$, hence is a single literal, so the composed function is one
DNF gate or its negation. Under a Bernoulli random restriction with parameter
$\mathrm{composedDelta}\,l\,l\,2$, the probability that the restricted function has
decision-tree depth exceeding $t$ is at most
\[
s_{\mathrm{rem}}\cdot\Bigl(\tfrac12\Bigr)^{l} + \Bigl(\tfrac12\Bigr)^{t}
+ s_{\mathrm{rem}}\cdot e^{-n/(120 l)} + e^{-n/(120 l)},
\]
under the hypotheses $0 < l$, $0 < n$, $c_{\mathrm{top}}.\mathrm{depth}+2\le 2$,
$c_{\mathrm{top}}.\mathrm{size}\le s_{\mathrm{rem}}$, $\mathrm{data.width}\le l$, and
$0 < s_{\mathrm{rem}}$.
